best_for: People who help family and friends with their computers from afar and want a quick connection, and who know that work use needs a paid license.
description:
AnyDesk is a remote desktop app from AnyDesk Software GmbH. It lets you see and control another computer, or let someone else control yours, for a quick fix or for regular access to your own machines.

Each device gets an AnyDesk ID, or a friendlier alias, and you type that address to start a session. While connected you can share the screen, send files and copy and paste between the two computers, and record the session. Favorites and Recent Sessions keep the machines you reach most often a click away, and a Discovered list shows other AnyDesk computers on the same network, so you need not swap IDs.

points.title: Free only for personal use
points.text: AnyDesk's terms limit the free version to personal, non-commercial use. Anything for your job, your business or pay needs a license, and AnyDesk may check free usage and suspend it.

points.title: Free sessions time out
points.text: Free sessions have a time limit. You can reconnect as often as you like, and a paid license removes the timeouts.

points.title: Runs without installing
points.text: The download can run straight away as a portable app, handy for a one-off support call. Unattended access and system integration need a full install.

points.title: Linux needs Xorg for incoming
points.text: To be controlled, a Linux machine must run an Xorg session; Wayland works only for outgoing connections. AnyDesk cannot run as root, and officially supports Ubuntu 18.04, Debian 9, RHEL 8 and Mint 20 or newer, plus Raspberry Pi OS.

points.title: The Flatpak trails the official build
points.text: The Flatpak listed here is 8.0.4, a Flathub build that Flathub does not mark as verified. AnyDesk's own changelog shows Linux at 8.1.1 as of November 19, 2026.

points.title: Old versions can be switched off
points.text: The terms let AnyDesk deactivate outdated versions after six weeks of notice. Each platform here lists only the current release, so stay current rather than plan on downgrading.

points.title: Windows and Mac downloads
points.text: The Windows download is a single installer for the whole machine. The Mac app is a universal disk image for Intel and Apple silicon.
